Open Start and type your company name and your own targets in the yellow cells: the margin you want, your lowest margin, the rating you want, the reply days, the repeat customer share and the growth you plan.

Products lists the 24 products with price, cost and status. The list margin, the age, the revenue, profit and margin of the last 12 months, the units, the rating and the checks fill in from the sales and review sheets.
Product month sales holds the units, revenue and costs of each product by month and channel. The total cost, the margin and the margin share fill in, and the dashboard and charts read this sheet.

Reviews and Review topics follow what customers say. Each review gets the days to reply and a check against your reply window; the rating and the topic charts show where the scent, the burn or the packaging lets you down.

Product ideas, New product trials, Sample feedback and Waitlist run new products from the first idea to the launch: expected margin, trial sell-through (units sold as a share of units made), tester scores and customers waiting.
Campaigns and Campaign results show the spend, the orders, the revenue and the return on spend of each campaign; Newsletter sends and Photo shoots show what each send and each shoot cost and brought.
Customers and Repeat customers by cohort show who orders again, who has not ordered for months and how the share of repeat customers changes by first order month.

Seasonal plan turns last year's units and the demand factor of each month into the units to make next year; Gift set ideas shows the margin of each set, and Competitor watch compares prices for 100 g.
Retire list records your decision on slow products and checks the live units and margin; Channels and Team hold the fees, the payout days and the phones that the messages use.

Use the 14 calculators before you decide: margin, mix, rating, reply time, repeat rate, customer lifetime value, campaign return, go or stop, seasonal stock, gift set, sell-through, retire or keep, newsletter payback and a what-if grid.

One row for each expense with the date, category, supplier, invoice number, amount and the day you paid; the month and the paid check fill in, and the budget and monthly profit sheets read this sheet.
Hours and pay of each team member by week
One row for each person and week with the work kind, the hours and the hourly rate; the pay and the phone fill in, and the monthly profit sheet adds the pay up.
Orders, sales, fees and shipping cost by channel and month
One row for each month and channel with the orders, the sales, the fees and the shipping cost; the net sales and the average order fill in.
One row for each product, month and channel with units, revenue and the costs; the total cost, the margin and the margin share fill in, and the profit by product charts read this sheet.
Profit of each channel in each of the last months
One row for each month and channel with the revenue, the cost of goods, the fees, the shipping lost and the labour in the product cost; the profit, the margin and the margin check fill in.
Profit of each fair and market after all its costs
One row for each fair or market with the sales and the costs; the month, the event cost, the profit and the result fill in, and a fair still to come shows no profit.
One row for each payout with the gross amount, the fees, the expected day and the day it arrived; the net amount, the days still waiting and the payout check fill in so a late payout stands out.
Tax payments with due dates and timing
One row for each tax payment with the period, the amount, the due date and the day you paid; the days to the due date and the timing check fill in so nothing is paid late.
Sales tax collected, remitted and still owed each month
One row for each month with the taxable sales, the rate, the tax collected and the amount and day remitted; the tax owed and the status fill in. Check your own local rules.
Money the owner takes out each month against a safe level
One row for each month with the draw and the day it was taken; the average profit of the last three months, the safe draw after your tax set-aside and the check fill in.
Planned and actual spending in six budget lines
One row for each month and budget line with the planned amount; the actual amount comes from the Expenses sheet, and the gap, the gap share and the check fill in.
Tools and display items with cost, life and yearly cost
One row for each item with the day bought, the cost, the life in years and the value at the end of its life; the yearly cost, the age, the value today and the status fill in.
Costs that come every month with the due day
One row for each fixed cost with the monthly amount, the due day and the supplier; the yearly amount, the next due date, the days to it and the share of all fixed costs fill in.
Revenue, cost of goods, running costs and profit by quarter
One row for each quarter; the figures come from the monthly profit and loss sheet, and the quarters still to come are planned from the same quarter last year with your growth.
Monthly profit and loss with cost of goods and net profit
One row for each month; type only the packaging cost, and the sales, costs, cost per unit, net profit and the margin checks fill in from the other sheets.
Wholesale invoices with the balance and the days late
One row for each wholesale invoice with the issue date, the due date, the amount and the payment; the balance, the days late and the check fill in, and only an unpaid invoice counts as late.
Bank lines matched to your records
One row for each bank line with the date, the description and the amount, with a tick when you matched it to a record; the days open and the check fill in, and money out is a negative amount.
The 24 products with price, cost and profit
One row for each product with the retail price and the unit cost; the list margin, the units, revenue and profit of the last 12 months and the margin check fill in from the product month sheet.

Open Start and type your company name and your own targets in the yellow cells: the cash floor, the owner draw, the share of profit you set aside, the sales tax rate, the margins you want and the days that raise a warning.
Profit and loss by month is the heart of the workbook: type only the packaging cost, and the sales, costs, cost for each unit, net profit and the margin checks fill in.

Expenses, Labour entries and Product month sales hold the rows behind the figures. Add a new expense or a labour entry and the monthly profit, the budget and the quarterly summary update by themselves.
Cash shows the opening cash, the money in and out in seven groups and the closing cash each month against your cash floor. The cash forecast calculator looks eight weeks ahead.

Sales by channel by month, Channel profit and Event profit show where the money is made and lost: each channel keeps its fees, shipping and labour, and each fair its stall fee, helper, travel and cost of goods.

Channel payouts lists every payout with the gross, the fees, the day you expect it and the day it arrived; a payout that is late is flagged. Bank reconciliation matches the bank lines to your records.

Tax rows, Sales tax by month and Owner draw follow the tax payments, the sales tax collected and still owed, and the draw against a safe level. Check your own local rules and ask your accountant for the rates and the dates.

Budget compares the planned amount of six lines with the actual amount from the Expenses sheet; Fixed costs lists what you pay every month; Equipment and assets gives the yearly cost and the value today of each item.
Wholesale receivables shows each wholesale invoice with its balance and the days late, counting only invoices that are not paid. Quarterly summary adds the months up for you and your accountant.

Use the 14 calculators before you decide: profit and loss, break-even, cash forecast, runway, safe draw, set-aside, sales tax, channels, cost per unit, budget, equipment, price rise, payouts and a what-if grid.
